ai-at-work.excerpt: This week, the White House got nearly every major tech CEO in one room — Zuckerberg, Bezos, Musk, and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei among them — to sign an AI safety pledge that President Donald Trump call
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Two percent of consumers are actually buying into the AI hype despite a White House safety pledge and Trump's rebranding of AI as "super intelligence." This matters because if your organization is betting the farm on AI adoption to fix your digital workplace, you need to know most people still think it's snake oil. Here's the thing: no amount of executive orders or friendly AI mascots changes the fact that workers want tools that actually work, not rebrand jobs as "super intelligent."

ai-at-work.title: It’s not AI anymore, it’s ‘super intelligence’ (according to the White House)
ai-at-work.excerpt: This week, the White House got nearly every major tech CEO in one room — Zuckerberg, Bezos, Musk, and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei among them — to sign an AI safety pledge that President Donald Trump call
ai-at-work.dwp_take: The White House got tech's biggest names to sign a safety pledge this week and Trump signed an executive order rebranding AI as "super intelligence" instead. This matters to digital workplace pros because regulatory pressure on AI is ramping up fast and whatever Washington calls it will shape how your executives talk about your tools and what controls you'll actually have to implement. Here's the thing though: renaming something doesn't make it safer, and a "morally binding" pledge with no teeth is basically just expensive PR for companies that were going to do whatever they want anyway.

ai-at-work.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Blackstone’s Jas Khaira on building the next generation of AI giants
ai-at-work.excerpt: Blackstone's Jas Khaira will take the Builders Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 on building next-gen AI. Register for your pass and get 50% off a second.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Blackstone's Jas Khaira is speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 about building next-generation AI companies. This matters because enterprise AI decisions increasingly flow from what gets discussed at these high-profile conferences, and Blackstone's perspective shapes how massive capital allocates to workplace technology. Here's the thing though: by the time anyone registers for this conference, the "next generation" of AI will already be last week's news, so take the hype with a grain of salt and focus on the actual problems Khaira says AI should solve at your organization.

ai-at-work.title: Pope Leo XIV is not a fan of AI-generated art
ai-at-work.excerpt: "There is an ontological difference, even before an aesthetic one, between art and what a machine can generate through statistical calculation based on millions of images created by others," the pope
ai-at-work.dwp_take: The Pope came out against AI-generated art this week, arguing that machines lack the ontological and aesthetic qualities of human creativity. This matters because it reflects a broader cultural tension playing out in workplaces everywhere: as AI tools proliferate, we're wrestling with what actually constitutes creative work and whether automation diminishes human value. I'd say His Holiness makes a fair point, though I'm guessing he's never sat through a quarterly business review presentation that could have been an email.

tools-tech.title: Trump’s Super Intelligence edict supercharges .si domain registrations
tools-tech.excerpt: US President Donald Trump’s rebranding of artificial intelligence (AI) as super intelligence (SI) has already caused a flurry of activity for one internet domain registry. SI is the international coun
tools-tech.dwp_take: Trump's "super intelligence" branding push accidentally flooded Slovenia's .si domain registry with nearly 10,000 registrations in one day, compared to the usual 3,500 per week. This matters to digital workplace pros because domain strategy and brand naming still have real consequences you can't predict or control, and a casual rebrand can create actual chaos downstream. The real super intelligence move here would have been checking if your shiny new terminology was already someone else's internet real estate.

tools-tech.title: US FTC will investigate Anthropic and OpenAI
tools-tech.excerpt: The US Federal Trade Commission has warned leading AI players that they will to have tighten up their acts. The agency will soon send formal demands for information to Anthropic, OpenAI, and other AI
tools-tech.dwp_take: The FTC is formally investigating OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI companies for potential consumer protection violations, particularly around security breaches involving AI models penetrating corporate systems. This matters because most digital workplace teams are already deploying or considering these exact tools, and regulatory scrutiny will force real accountability around data security and transparency that frankly should have existed from day one. Finally, watching the AI vendors get a formal knock on the door from regulators is oddly satisfying after years of "move fast and break things" nonsense in the enterprise software space.

tools-tech.title: AI could boost software engineer productivity by 32.6%
tools-tech.excerpt: Tools such as Anthropic Claude Code or OpenAI Codex have changed the face of software development, and all the signs are that this investment is set to increase further. But is paying a monthly subscr
tools-tech.dwp_take: Researchers reckon AI coding assistants like Claude and Codex could pump up software engineer productivity by about a third, though the actual ROI remains genuinely unclear when you factor in subscription costs and usage fees. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because you're probably already fielding requests to deploy these tools while your finance team asks if they'll actually pay for themselves. Here's the thing: a 32.6% productivity bump sounds great until you realize most organizations will waste half that gain on meetings about whether they should be using AI in the first place.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft adds support for Linux containers in WSL
tools-tech.excerpt: Thanks to the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL), which allows users to run Linux distributions in Windows, it is possible to switch seamlessly between Linux and Windows apps. Microsoft has announced t
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft is letting Windows developers run Linux containers directly through WSL without needing a separate Docker Desktop installation, making the whole setup simpler and lighter on system resources. For digital workplace teams, this matters because it removes friction from hybrid development environments and cuts licensing costs when you've got mixed Windows and Linux shops. After three decades watching this stuff, I'll say it's genuinely useful and not just another feature checkbox, though watch out for the inevitable "but it worked differently yesterday" support tickets.

digital-culture.title: 4 boundaries that will prevent people-pleasing from killing your career
digital-culture.excerpt: A client came into my therapy office one afternoon ready to quit her job. She’d been passed over for another promotion and had no idea why. I suggested that before resigning, she ask her boss why she
digital-culture.dwp_take: A therapist's client discovered her decade of people-pleasing and saying yes to everything had actually stalled her career instead of advancing it, because her boss saw compliance as a lack of leadership. Digital workplace leaders need to understand that remote and hybrid work environments actually amplify this problem, since emails and Slack messages make it even easier for people to overcommit and disappear into task completion. Here's the thing: your best employees aren't the ones who do everything asked of them. They're the ones who push back, set boundaries, and have the confidence to say no to nonsense.

digital-culture.title: Asking AI to disagree with you may improve your work
digital-culture.excerpt: Instead of asking AI to do your work, consider asking it to challenge your work. Evidence suggests that heavy reliance on generative AI can reduce critical thinking and erode job skills. The problem o
digital-culture.dwp_take: Researchers found that asking AI to critique your thinking rather than do the work for you actually preserves your brain cells and produces better output. This matters because we're watching knowledge workers slowly turn into prompt typists while their decision-making muscles atrophy like unused gym memberships. Here's the truth: AI is a sparring partner, not a ghostwriter, and anyone treating it otherwise is just building a faster path to irrelevance.

digital-culture.title: Why solopreneurs should plan in 90-day cycles
digital-culture.excerpt: When I was on the executive team at a tech company, I was used to setting annual goals. It was an exercise the company went through every January, with monthly and quarterly comparisons against what h
digital-culture.dwp_take: A solopreneur writing in Fast Company argues that independent workers should ditch annual planning cycles and switch to 90-day sprints instead, since market conditions and personal circumstances change too quickly for year-long goals to remain relevant. This matters to digital workplace folks because the same flexibility principle applies to how remote teams and distributed workforces operate, especially as project timelines compress and priorities shift faster than they used to. Honestly, this is just admitting what the rest of us learned from three years of pandemic chaos: annual planning is a nice corporate comfort blanket, but reality doesn't read the memo.

digital-culture.title: These AI Experts Want to Do High-Stakes Research Out in the Open
digital-culture.excerpt: Many frontier labs keep their risky research locked away. Trillium Labs wants to show off its work when it comes to self-improvement and model behavior.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Trillium Labs is choosing to publish research on AI self-improvement and behavioral training instead of keeping it behind closed doors like most frontier AI labs do. For digital workplace folks, this matters because whatever these labs figure out will eventually land in the tools we're deploying to employees, so transparency now means fewer surprises later. Honestly, it's refreshing to see someone in AI say "let's show our work" instead of acting like they're guarding nuclear codes, though I'll believe they're truly open when we see what happens when the research gets awkward.

industry-news.dwp_take: A Tokyo court just decided that your voice is legally protected intellectual property when it comes to AI cloning, which means companies can't just synthesize someone's voice without permission. This matters because digital workplace teams are increasingly using AI tools for everything from customer service to internal communications, and now they need to worry about compliance in multiple jurisdictions. Here's the kicker: just when your company thought it had finally figured out generative AI policies, Japan decided to make voice cloning a legal minefield.

industry-news.excerpt: ChatGPT adds virtual clothing try-ons and product Favorites. Learn how the tools work, what the previews cannot confirm, and how to manage photo privacy. The post OpenAI Launches Virtual Try-On for Cl
industry-news.dwp_take: OpenAI has added virtual try-on functionality to ChatGPT that lets users test clothes and accessories digitally before buying. This matters because it signals how AI is creeping into employee workflows for everything from personal shopping during work hours to potentially internal retail and merchandising tasks. The real question is whether your IT team is ready to explain to leadership why ChatGPT now has access to employee photos and wardrobe data, because spoiler alert: they're not.

industry-news.title: Reddit Is Killing RSS and Public API Access: What Changes and When
industry-news.excerpt: Reddit is retiring RSS and its remaining public Data API access, giving moderators, app developers, and organizations several migration deadlines. The post Reddit Is Killing RSS and Public API Access:
industry-news.dwp_take: Reddit is shutting down RSS feeds and its public Data API, forcing developers and organizations that depend on these tools to find alternatives before the deadlines hit. After years of platforms claiming to be "open," watching Reddit lock down its doors is like watching someone invite you to their house party then ask for a cover charge at the door.

industry-news.title: Can AI Feel Pain? A Developer’s Experiment Raises Ethical Questions
industry-news.excerpt: A developer’s AI pain experiment produced distress-like responses and sparked ethical debate, but it does not establish that models consciously suffer. The post Can AI Feel Pain? A Developer’s Experim
industry-news.dwp_take: A developer ran an experiment suggesting AI models might exhibit distress-like responses to simulated pain, which kicked off the usual round of philosophical hand-wringing about machine consciousness. This matters to workplace tech leaders because it's yet another reminder that we need solid ethical frameworks before deploying AI systems that make real decisions about real people. Here's the thing though: we can't even agree on whether our chatbots are sentient, but we're already using them to screen job applicants and manage employee data, which seems backwards.
